entries.topic: The Lateran Treaty: how a city-state was made in 1929

claims.text: Signed 11 February 1929 at the Lateran Palace by Benito Mussolini for King Victor Emmanuel III and Cardinal Pietro Gasparri for Pope Pius XI; ratified by the Italian Parliament on 7 June 1929. Three instruments: a treaty, a concordat and a financial convention.

Background: Italy occupied and annexed Latium and Rome in 1870; the 1871 Law of Guarantees offered the pope the use of the Vatican and Lateran palaces and an annual income, which the Holy See refused, and popes regarded themselves as prisoners in the Vatican.
Financial convention: Italy paid 750 million lire at once plus consolidated 5% bearer bonds of a nominal 1,000 million lire, settling the Holy See's claims from the 1870 losses.

Article 2: Italy recognizes the sovereignty of the Holy See in international matters as an inherent attribute. Article 3: full ownership, exclusive dominion and sovereign jurisdiction of the Holy See over the Vatican; St Peter's Square stays open to the public and subject to supervision by Italian police. Article 4: no Italian government interference.

Article 6: Italy must ensure an adequate water supply, rail links and connections by telegraph, telephone, wireless, broadcasting and post. Articles 13–16: Holy See ownership of the basilicas of St John Lateran, Santa Maria Maggiore and St Paul, and the papal palace of Castel Gandolfo, with diplomatic-style immunity and exemption from expropriation. Article 20: goods for Vatican institutions cross Italy free of customs.

Article 22: at the Holy See's request Italy prosecutes crimes committed in Vatican City. Article 24: the Holy See will take no part in temporal conflicts between other states, and Vatican City is neutral and inviolable territory. Article 26: the Holy See declares the Roman Question settled and recognizes the Kingdom of Italy with Rome as its capital.

The 1984 revision of the concordat (signed 18 February 1984, in force 3 June 1985) ended Catholicism's status as sole state religion and replaced state financing with the otto per mille (0.8% of income tax).

entries.topic: How Vatican City runs day to day

claims.text: The pope holds the fullness of legislative, executive and judicial power under the Fundamental Law of Vatican City State promulgated by Pope Francis on 13 May 2023; the Pontifical Commission keeps legislative power for the city, its cardinal president is also President of the Governorate, and lay men and women may now be appointed members for five-year terms. The Commission deliberates the annual budget and a three-year plan and submits them to the pope.

Sources of law: a law of 1 October 2008 (in force 1 January 2009) makes canon law the first source; Italian law is received only where it does not conflict with canon law, divine law or the Lateran agreements; the 1889 Zanardelli penal code remains in use. Courts: a single judge, a three-judge Tribunal, a Court of Appeal, and a Court of Cassation of cardinals. The Governorate president acts much like a mayor, running the museums, post, gardens and shop, and may call on the Gendarmerie.

Citizenship is by office (jus officii), not birth: cardinals, Holy See diplomats and those living in the city because of their work, with spouses and children; it usually ends with the appointment, and anyone left stateless becomes Italian under the Lateran Treaty. As of 26 June 2023: 618 citizens and 764 inhabitants.

No taxes; revenue from donations, stamps, coins, medals, museum admissions and publications; no prison beyond pre-trial cells, convicts serve sentences in Italian prisons at Vatican cost; St Peter's Square normally patrolled by Italian police; no passport controls from Italy; own post (1929), telephone system, .va domain, radio, railway spur and heliport.

The euro: Monetary Agreement with the EU signed 17 December 2009 (in force 1 January 2010, replacing the 2000 agreement): Vatican City may use the euro and mint limited coins (made by Italy's state mint) and must adopt EU anti-money-laundering and anti-counterfeiting rules.

entries.topic: The Holy See: Curia, diplomacy and budget

claims.text: Praedicate Evangelium, promulgated 19 March 2022 and in force 5 June 2022, reorganized the Roman Curia into 16 dicasteries and allows any member of the faithful, including lay people, to lead one.

As of early 2026 the Holy See had full diplomatic relations with 184 states plus the EU and the Order of Malta; 93 missions are accredited in Rome and the Holy See has 128 nunciatures; Pope Leo XIV addressed the diplomatic corps on 9 January 2026.

2024 consolidated Holy See accounts (Secretariat for the Economy, published 26 November 2025): operating income €1.23 billion, operating expenses €1.275 billion, operational deficit €44.4 million, overall surplus €1.6 million after investment returns, asset sales and donations; nunciatures took 10% of apostolic-mission spending.

Pietro Parolin was appointed Secretary of State on 31 August 2013 and took office 15 October 2013; earlier (from 30 November 2002) he was Undersecretary for Relations with States and in December 2008 led the Holy See delegation to the Permanent Bilateral Commission with Israel.

entries.topic: The papacy's money: from the Rothschild loans to the IOR

claims.text: The Holy See's 1831 agreement with the Rothschilds, signed 30 November 1831, gave Pope Gregory XVI a 5% loan of £400,000 in 1832; Alessandro Torlonia negotiated for the Holy See with James de Rothschild, who became papal banker; a secret clause obliged the Holy See to inform the Rothschilds before borrowing elsewhere and prefer them on equal terms; a second loan followed under Pius IX in the early 1850s.

Through Metternich the Rothschilds asked the pope for concessions for Jews in the Papal States: removal of extra taxes, of the ban on taking property out of the ghetto, of professional restrictions, and easing of court rules. Alfred de Vigny wrote that "a Jew now reigns over the Pope and Christianity".

The IOR was founded 27 June 1942 by Pius XII; it is a canonical foundation with no shareholders, not a Curia department or central bank. After losing Italian tax exemption in 1968 the Holy See hired Michele Sindona. In the Banco Ambrosiano collapse (1982) the IOR, a 10% shareholder, denied legal liability, acknowledged "moral involvement" and paid US$224 million to creditors.

Reforms: Financial Intelligence Authority created 30 December 2010; first Moneyval report July 2012 (9 of 16 core standards met); first IOR annual report 1 October 2013 and closure of about 1,300 accounts; 2019 statutes; rescript of 23 August 2022 moving all Holy See financial resources to the IOR.

IOR 2025 results (Vatican News, 11 May 2026): net income €51 million, client assets €5.9 billion, Tier 1 ratio 71.9%, dividend to the pope €24.3 million; François Pauly succeeded Jean-Baptiste de Franssu as president.

François Pauly was named CEO of the Edmond de Rothschild group in June 2021, succeeding Vincent Taupin, after careers at Dexia, Sal. Oppenheim and BIL; he left the CEO post around 2023. His IOR appointment was proposed 12 December 2025, approved by the cardinals 28 January 2026, announced 25 March 2026, effective after the 28 April 2026 board meeting.

The London building at 60 Sloane Avenue was sold in 2022 at an estimated loss of about €140 million. On 16 December 2023 the Vatican tribunal convicted Cardinal Angelo Becciu of embezzlement and sentenced him to 5½ years. On 17 March 2026 the Court of Appeal found a "relative nullity" from the prosecution's failure to disclose investigative documents and ordered part of the proceedings renewed; on 29 October 2026 it set preliminary hearings for 26–29 January 2027.

entries.topic: Whose theology: Catholic teaching and Protestant dispensationalism

claims.text: Catechism of the Catholic Church §676 says the Church "has rejected even modified forms" of the falsification of the kingdom to come "under the name of millenarianism", citing DS 3839 (the Holy Office's 1944 decree that mitigated millenarianism cannot safely be taught).

The Scofield Reference Bible was first published in 1909 by Oxford University Press, revised 1917, sold over two million copies by the end of the Second World War, promoted dispensationalism and shaped the Christian Zionist movement, including John Hagee's Christians United for Israel.

The 1985 Notes of the Commission for Religious Relations with the Jews (Rome, 24 June 1985), §33: the existence of the State of Israel and its political options "should be envisaged not in a perspective which is in itself religious, but in their reference to the common principles of international law".
"The Gifts and the Calling of God are Irrevocable" (10 December 2015): the Church "neither conducts nor supports any specific institutional mission work directed towards Jews".
JTA reported in 1985 that a Jewish group was unhappy with the Vatican document because it failed to consider the religious significance of Israel.

entries.topic: The Holy See and Zionism, then Israel, 1904–2026

claims.text: 25 January 1904: Pius X received Herzl and said "We cannot prevent the Jews from going to Jerusalem but we could never sanction it." 4 May 1917: Benedict XV received Nahum Sokolow and said the problem of the holy places "is of extraordinary importance for us".

15 May 1922: Cardinal Gasparri's note to the League of Nations said the Holy See could not agree to "the Jews being given a privileged and preponderant position in Palestine vis-à-vis the Catholics"; the League approved the Mandate on 22 July 1922.
May 1943: Cardinal Maglione wrote to the apostolic delegate Cicognani that Palestine "under Jewish predominance, would bring new and grave international problems".

The Holy See avoided interfering in the 29 November 1947 partition vote, probably to protect internationalisation of Jerusalem; Pius XII called for Jerusalem to receive "an international character" (In multiplicibus, 24 October 1948) and "a juridical statute internationally guaranteed" (15 April 1949). The 1949 encyclical asked help for refugees and did not mention Israel.

Irish government files released 2004: Spain proposed in December 1948 that Catholic envoys press for Catholic governance of Jerusalem; Italy, Spain, Portugal and Ireland held talks at the Vatican in April 1949; the initiative stalled because the Vatican was reluctant to reveal its position and the four would not act without its backing; the Holy See avoided demands that "might lead to the Vatican itself being saddled with responsibility for promoting further disturbance in Palestine".
UNGA Resolution 303 (IV), 9 December 1949, 38–14–7, restated a permanent international regime for Jerusalem; Israel, the US and UK voted against.

Lewy (2009): the Holy See had advocated international status for Jerusalem and Bethlehem since 1937; Bialer's research suggests it doubted Israel would survive; the 1964 papal visit did not address Israel's president by title; after 1967 a pragmatic policy grew alongside declaratory non-recognition; the archives of the relevant papacies are open but Vatican attitudes are still known mainly from Jewish sources.

5 January 1964: Paul VI's pilgrimage to the Holy Land. 28 October 1965: Nostra Aetate. 15 January 1973: Paul VI received Golda Meir. September 1987: sources close to John Paul II said there was "no longer any theological obstacle" to relations. 30 December 1993: Fundamental Agreement signed by Msgr Claudio Maria Celli and Yossi Beilin; relations established 19 January 1994; in force 10 March 1994; ambassadors exchanged after the Cairo Agreement of 4 May 1994. March 2000: John Paul II's visit, Yad Vashem 23 March.

Legal Personality Agreement 10 November 1997; the economic and fiscal agreement on Church property and taxes was still not concluded as of June 2019; the Knesset has not incorporated the Fundamental Agreement into Israeli domestic law.
Holy See–State of Palestine Comprehensive Agreement signed 26 June 2015, in force 2 January 2016 (Preamble and 32 articles).

Leo XIV received President Herzog on 4 September 2025; the Holy See called for release of hostages, a permanent ceasefire, humanitarian access and the two-state solution as "the only way out of the ongoing war". On 1 December 2025 aboard the papal plane: "We are also friends with Israel and we are seeking to be a mediating voice"; Israel "does not yet accept" the two-state proposal. In October 2025 Leo backed Cardinal Parolin after Israel rebuked the Holy See's Gaza comments.

entries.topic: The Pius XII archives and the "front" question

claims.text: The Vatican opened the archives of Pius XII's pontificate on 2 March 2020; they closed soon after for Italy's COVID-19 lockdown and reopened with limited access.

David Kertzer, The Pope at War (Random House, 2022), drawing on the archives: Pius XII's silence stemmed mainly from "his priority for protecting the institutional church"; during the 16 October 1943 roundup in Rome the Vatican did not protest to the German ambassador but sought the release of baptised detainees and Catholic spouses.
Rioli (2017): some members of the Latin Catholic Church of Jerusalem argued an analogy between Nazism and Zionism across 1947–49, the 1950s and the Eichmann trial.

Resolution 181 passed 33–13–10 on 29 November 1947; 13 of the 33 yes votes came from Latin American states (Bolivia, Brazil, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Ecuador, Guatemala, Haiti, Nicaragua, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay, Venezuela); Cuba voted no; Argentina, Chile, Colombia, El Salvador, Honduras and Mexico abstained.

A 1959 study attributes Latin America's role mainly to its delegates' activism (Zuloaga of Venezuela, García Granados of Guatemala, Rodríguez Fabregat of Uruguay, Aranha of Brazil); its summary does not credit Vatican influence.

entries.topic: The historic churches of Jerusalem on Christian Zionism

claims.text: Jerusalem Declaration on Christian Zionism, 22 August 2006, signed by Latin (Catholic) Patriarch Michel Sabbah, Syriac Orthodox Archbishop Swerios Malki Mourad, Anglican Bishop Riah Abu El-Assal and Lutheran Bishop Munib Younan: Christian Zionism is a "false teaching that corrupts the biblical message of love, justice, and reconciliation."

17 January 2026 statement of the Patriarchs and Heads of Churches in Jerusalem calls Christian Zionism among "damaging ideologies" that "wound the unity of the faithful" and constitute "interference in the internal life of the churches"; US Ambassador Mike Huckabee criticized the statement.
